plain: "Most of that improvement had nothing to do with the queue" (overstates the notes; A itself says parallel workers helped)
"Finding the bug took two weeks" (the notes say the bug cost two weeks, not that finding it did)
"Invoices go out on time again" (implied but not stated)
"Once you have a queue, you have retries" (presented as the cause of the double-counting)
"What I'd tell anyone planning a similar move:"
"→ Before you add parallelism, check how your job uses memory. You might not need parallelism."

why.human: B is tight and concrete. It reads like an engineering manager reporting what happened and then asking a pointed question. A uses the usual LinkedIn template: arrow-bullet lessons, 'What I'd tell anyone…', 'Tell me in the comments', and a block of hashtags.
why.useful: B gives every key fact (the cause, the fix, the idempotency bug, who did the work) in less space. Its closing question about deduping retries with a run id is specific enough to get the comments from practitioners that the manager asked for. A's takeaways are mostly generic advice. A also says the improvement 'had nothing to do with the queue' and then says parallel workers helped, which contradicts itself.
